member.name: T:Lumio.GameRuntime.Simulation.Warmup.TickPathWarmup
member.summary: Pays the first-execution (JIT) cost of the Tick path before Ready (ADR-118 decision 5) without running a Tick (decision 6). The method set is derived, not listed: starting from the roots it follows every call the IL can make — resolving generic instantiations exactly and virtual calls against the types that can be live — and then asks the runtime to compile each reached method with . No Tick code runs: no world, entity, voxel, tick counter or persistence is touched, and a prepared static constructor is compiled but not run. Code outside the Tick does run: resolving the IL loads the assemblies it references, including ones the Tick itself never loads, which raises the host's AssemblyLoad / AssemblyResolve on the Priming thread; and creating an entry point or preparing a method activates its module, which runs that assembly's [ModuleInitializer]. Both happen while SimulationSession.Prime holds the session's gate.
member.remarks:
Virtual dispatch uses two receiver sources. For slots declared by application assemblies (the engine and the gameplay) every loaded concrete type that implements the slot is a candidate, because such receivers — the registry, components, the admission adapter — are usually created outside the Tick path. For slots declared by the shared framework (object, IEquatable<T>, IEnumerable<T>…) only types the path itself allocates are candidates; the whole application implements those, and taking all of them would compile most of the process. Framework method bodies are only followed for instantiations over value types: shared reference-type code and non-generic framework code are precompiled (ReadyToRun), while a value-type instantiation such as Dictionary<NetEntityId, int> exists only once JIT compiles it. The netstandard2.1 build does no warm-up (follow-up 4, R-00763). This is not the same gap for its two hosts:
IL2CPP has no JIT: it ahead-of-time compiles the whole managed program at build time, so "first-execution JIT cost" does not exist there to prepay. A no-op is correct by construction, not an omission.
Mono does have a JIT, so in principle a no-op leaves a real first-Tick cost on a Mono host. Implementing it anyway was rejected for this PR: this derivation depends on CoreCLR-specific behavior that has never been exercised under Mono in this repository — 's actual JIT-triggering effect, RuntimeMethodHandle/TypeHandle pointer identity used to dedupe shared generic code (the internal MethodKey and RootsKey), and whether MethodBase.GetMethodBody().GetILAsByteArray() survives Mono's own trimming/AOT preprocessing the way it does under CoreCLR. Shipping an unverified port would report a coverage number nobody measured, which is exactly the failure mode ADR-118 step 6 exists to catch (the Linux AVX2 gap in this same file was only found by measuring, not by reasoning about the code). No netstandard2.1 host in this repository runs on Mono today — the target exists for forward Unity compatibility, not a wired-up host — so there is nothing to measure yet.
Decision: leave the netstandard2.1 no-op as is, but as a documented, load-bearing decision rather than silence. When a Mono host is wired up in this repository, it goes through the same measure-first discipline as any other platform before Prime is trusted to cover it — the ADR-118 step-6 fixture, not a speculative implementation.
